_status: MEASURED 2026-10-09 on a4aae82, the FIRST measurement after the #169 frame fix. All three sequences run sequentially by tools/rerun_baseline.sh at 1x with the machine left alone: 0 robot_localization starvation events on all three, achieved filter rate 99.9 to 103.1 Hz, and all six 3D-vs-XY pairs internally consistent, which the previous file was not. THE CONTROL IS NOT COMPARABLE TO THE PRE-FIX ENTRIES and that is expected, not a fault: #169 changed the wheel-odometry yaw rate the player publishes and BOTH filters consume it, so the control moved +148.1%, -1.2% and -75.3% on the three sequences. The old values are kept per sequence under superseded_pre_frame_fix. n=1 on two of the three, n=2 on 2012-06-15 (78.112 and 82.011, 5.0% apart, inside its documented 5.8% spread; control 45.772 and 45.864, 0.20% apart). Treat a move under ~6% on 2012-06-15 or 2012-08-20 as noise and ~1% as meaningful on 2013-04-05, as before. A 2026-10-08 note claiming that working on the machine during a playback moved the control 148% is WITHDRAWN: the paired runs above differ by 62 starvation events and 0.20% of control. See the 2026-10-08/09 section of tools/benchmark_regression.md.

2013-04-05.note: The frame fix is vindicated here. FusionCore 189.700 to 16.137, a 91.5% improvement, which lands near the 12.1 m of the May 2026 published snapshot and says the 189.7 was the frame bug rather than the filter. The control improved too, 266.700 to 65.776, so the win margin narrowed from 95% to 75.5%. FusionCore wins this one clearly.

_read_this_before_judging_any_regression: The 9x run-to-run spread is NOT universal, which an earlier note here implied. Measured over six unattended runs on 2026-09-12: 2012-06-15 repeats to 2.8%, 2012-08-20 to 4.6%, 2013-04-05 to 1.2%. The historical 32 m to 345 m range was all one sequence, 2013-04-05, and got generalised. So on these sequences a 5 to 10 percent change IS measurable and two runs are enough to see it. Keep the caution for a sequence whose spread has not been measured, and re-check it when adding one. robot_localization remains the control: if it moves more than about a percent between runs, the comparison is void whatever FusionCore did, and that check has already caught one wrong diagnosis (see issue #119).
_rerun_20261005: Re-run of the three sequences with baselines, on c263814, driven strictly sequentially with one playback per sequence feeding BOTH FusionCore and the robot_localization control. Results: 2012-06-15 VALID and confirming (control +0.01%), 2012-08-20 VALID and showing a regression (control -0.11%), 2013-04-05 VOID (control -4.40%, 20 rl_ekf update-rate misses with a worst case of 0.266 s against a 0.05 s budget, and a 75 min playback for 67.5 min of data). The 2013-04-05 arm was contended and is being re-run. NOTE THE PATTERN WORTH CHECKING: both VALID rows overstate FusionCore in the published README by almost exactly the same factor, 1.490x and 1.477x. Two independent sequences landing on the same ratio suggests something systematic rather than independent drift, and it is worth understanding before any published number is rewritten.
_frame_bug_20261006: EVERY ENTRY IN THIS FILE, AND EVERY NCLT NUMBER THIS PROJECT HAS PUBLISHED, WAS MEASURED WITH ISSUE #169 PRESENT. nclt_player.py converted the IMU from NCLT's NED-like body frame to ENU and did not convert the wheel odometry, so the encoder fed a yaw rate of the OPPOSITE SIGN to the gyro for the whole of every run. Proven on 2013-04-05 over 137,509 samples where both sources exceeded 0.08 rad/s: raw odometry against raw gyro disagree 0.0% of the time, raw odometry against the ENU-converted gyro disagree 100.0%, and with the fix they disagree 0.0%. Fixed 2026-10-06. WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT MEAN: the bug was real and is now gone, but its EFFECT on ATE is UNMEASURED. Do not claim the numbers will improve. The filter never diverged on it because imu.gyro_noise is tighter than encoder.yaw_noise, so it leaned on the gyro and spent gain rejecting the encoder on every turn, a quiet tax rather than a crash. CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS FILE: every baseline below is now pre-fix and is not comparable to a post-fix run. check_benchmark_regression.py will read any new run against a pre-fix reference and report nonsense. The whole set needs re-measuring before any of these are used to gate anything again. STILL OPEN AND SEPARATE: the magnitudes do not match either. The median |odom|/|imu| ratio over those same samples is 1.297, so NCLT's own wheel odometry over-reports rotation by about 30%. That is a scale or track-width term, not a frame convention, and the sign fix does not touch it.
